**Finding: MFN — compliant (preferred position).**

No most-favoured-nation obligation burdens Tri City National Bank. I searched independently for each formulation of the concept (most favoured/favored nation, "less favorable than", best/lowest price, other customers/financial institutions, right to match a competing offer or bid, standard price list comparisons) and read the complete fee architecture in Article 8 (8.1–8.14) plus Article 3 (Appointment). Nothing requires Customer to give M&I terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, or to match third-party offers.

Supporting points:
- **§ 8.1** fixes pricing by reference to the Fee Schedule only.
- **§ 8.9** runs the other way (discounts to Customer).
- **§ 8.14A** reverts to M&I's then-current standard published prices only following a Customer Event of Default, and reverts back on cure — a default pricing remedy, not an MFN mechanic, and not flagged here.

Because the preferred element ("Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor") is satisfied, I did not propose a redline. The absence of an MFN in *our* favour is a commercial opportunity, not a playbook deviation — we can raise a Customer-benefit best-pricing clause in negotiation if desired, but it is not required by this rule.
